title: Output Devices
subject: Computer Science
description: Projectors, screens, speakers, printers, 3D printers and actuators.
author: Erick

cards.back: Outputs text, numbers or images, and allows multiple people to view the same information.

cards.front: What surface does a projector need?
cards.back: A large, flat, white surface.
Can be used with a projector so the presenter doesn't block the projector.

cards.front: When does a projector need a brighter light?
cards.back: The further it is from the screen, and the brighter the environment it is used in. Brighter projectors cost more.

cards.front: Name two types of digital projector
cards.back: DLP projectors and LCD projectors.

cards.front: How does a DLP projector work?
cards.back: It uses a chip covered in millions of tiny mirrors (a DMD), one for each pixel. Each mirror tilts towards or away from the light to make its pixel light or dark. A spinning colour wheel (red, green and blue) adds the colour, and a lens projects the image onto the screen.
Digital Light Processing.

cards.front: How does an LCD projector work?
cards.back: A bright lamp's light is split by special mirrors into red, green and blue beams. Each beam passes through its own small LCD panel, which lets light through or blocks it for each pixel. A prism recombines the three colours and a lens projects the image onto the screen.
Liquid Crystal Display. Used in everything from calculators to large panel screens.

cards.front: Why does an LCD screen need a back light?
cards.back: So it can be seen easily.
Normally by fluorescent lights, which take time to warm up and give an uneven light, but more commonly these days by LEDs.

cards.front: What can LCD screens display, and how big are they?
cards.back: Multiple data types. They can be small for an individual (e.g. a smartphone) or very large for public information.

cards.front: Name three types of monitor or screen
cards.back: LCD screens, OLED screens and LED screen walls.

cards.front: How does an LCD screen work?
cards.back: Liquid crystals sit between layers of glass in front of a back light. Each pixel's crystals twist to block light or let it through, and red, green and blue filters give each pixel its colour.

cards.front: How does an OLED screen work?
cards.back: Each pixel is made of organic material that gives out its own light when an electric current passes through it, so no back light is needed.
Organic Light-Emitting Diode.
No back light is needed, so screens can be thinner, lighter and even flexible. Pixels can switch off completely for true black (better contrast).

cards.front: How does an LED screen wall work?
cards.back: It is built from many panels joined together. Each pixel is a group of tiny red, green and blue LEDs that give out their own light, making a very large, bright display.
Output sound, such as speech, music or warning beeps. They can be designed to fill a room or a whole stadium with sound.
Allow an individual to be the only one who hears the sound, so they don't disturb others and give a greater degree of privacy.

Digital sound data is converted into an analogue signal by a DAC and amplified. The current flows through a coil next to a magnet, making the coil and attached cone move back and forth. The vibrating cone pushes the air, making sound waves.
Digital-to-analogue convertor: converts digital data into an analogue signal, e.g. so a speaker or an actuator can use it.
A cheap printer that sprays ink onto paper. Ideal for photographs, but text can be blurry because the ink soaks into ordinary paper.
Uses toner. Ideal for text, giving a crisp, clear printout, but struggles to mix colours for images.

cards.front: What do printers output, and where are they used?
cards.back: Text, numbers or images. They can be small for receipts, used in the home or office, or produce large posters.

cards.front: How does an inkjet printer work?
cards.back: The paper is fed through a line at a time while a print head moves across it, firing tiny droplets of ink through nozzles (using heat to make a bubble, or a vibrating crystal) to build up the image.

cards.front: How does a laser printer work?
cards.back: A laser draws the page onto a rotating drum as a pattern of electric charge. Powdered toner sticks to the charged areas, is transferred onto the paper, and is then fused (melted) on by heated rollers.
Outputs 3D physical models. Used for rapid prototyping and to create bespoke (custom) products. The plastic can be brittle (easily breaks).
It builds an object layer by layer from a digital design (a CAD file), e.g. melting plastic and laying it down through a heated nozzle. Building up layers like this is called additive manufacturing.
Outputs movement. Can be used to control robots or a whole host of devices, motors or valves.
Very precise movement that is the same every time, and they don't need to rest. But they can be very expensive (over a million pounds for a factory robot).
It receives a signal from a computer or microprocessor (converted by a DAC if needed) and turns it into physical movement, e.g. a motor turning, a valve opening or a switch closing.
